Can you swim at Big Buddha Beach? | We don't recommend it. The water is shallow, muddy and often murky (especially in April–May), boats use the bay all day and broken glass has been reported in the sand. Swim at Choeng Mon, 10 minutes east, or use a beach-club pool.
Which pier do ferries to Koh Phangan leave from? | It depends on the operator. Lomprayah uses the Lomprayah pier, Seatran Discovery the Seatran pier, Songserm and Echo Travel Petcherat Marina, and the Haad Rin Queen the Big Buddha pier. All are loosely called Bangrak pier, so check the operator on your ticket.
Where does the Haad Rin Queen leave from? | From the Big Buddha pier at the eastern end of Bang Rak bay. The ferry costs 200 THB and sails at 10:30 and 17:00, taking about 50 minutes to Haad Rin; the Haad Rin Queen speedboat costs 500 THB.
Is Bang Rak noisy? | In the daytime, yes: planes on approach to Samui Airport pass low overhead and the piers are busy. Nights are quieter apart from the beach clubs. Light sleepers should stay in Choeng Mon or Maenam instead.
Is Bang Rak a good place to stay before an early ferry? | Yes, it is the most practical base for one or two nights: the ferry piers are on the doorstep and the airport is about 5 minutes away. It is not a good base for a beach holiday because the sea is poor for swimming.
How far is Bang Rak from the airport? | About 2–3 km, roughly 5 minutes by car. Airport taxis charge by zone, roughly 400–700 THB; Grab drivers meet you outside the airport pickup area.
What is the difference between Bang Rak and Big Buddha? | Bang Rak is the bay and village; Big Buddha (Wat Phra Yai) is the temple with the golden seated Buddha on the Koh Fan islet at the eastern end of the bay, open 07:00–18:30 and free. The beach is nicknamed Big Buddha Beach after it.
